purpose: Separate three possible bottlenecks behind the failed investment mutation-accessibility prediction: depleted standing variation, insufficient de novo mutation supply, and finite-population establishment.
scope: new prospective diagnostic after a failed preregistered experiment; no threshold-crossing rescue
primary_endpoint: absolute terminal-minus-initial investment change at year 400

predeclared_contrasts.standing_variation_effect: high-standing/equal-mutation minus low-standing/equal-mutation, averaged over histories and capacities
predeclared_contrasts.mutation_rescue_effect: low-standing/investment-accessible minus low-standing/equal-mutation, averaged over histories and capacities
predeclared_contrasts.capacity_modulation_of_mutation_rescue: mutation rescue at capacity 192 minus mutation rescue at capacity 48, averaged over histories

interpretation: standing only: response depends mainly on variation already present over this horizon
mutation rescue: de novo accessibility can restore response when standing variation is depleted
capacity modulation: mutation rescue is strengthened when finite-population filtering is weakened
none: the missing investment response is more likely due to selection geometry or another unmodelled genetic constraint under this parameterization

claim_boundary: This design was created after the failed Stage C and is a new prospective diagnostic, not a rescue of the failed threshold test.
No crossing threshold or horizon from the failed test is altered and re-labelled as confirmation.
Mutation rates/effect sizes and capacities are synthetic contrasts.
Investment remains an abstract pollinator-facing investment axis, not literal flower colour.
All cells and both visitor histories must be reported regardless of direction.
